rationale: reversefile is a small, I/O-bound Shootout C++ benchmark whose logic (line buffering, string handling, a reversal loop) is simple, so static profile features are sparse and the main goal is maximizing per-function transformation coverage rather than targeting heavy compute kernels. FLA and BCF get the highest SecurityGain because control-flow flattening and bogus-flow insertion are the strongest barriers to static/dynamic analysis of the reversal logic, and their runtime/size costs are acceptable here since the program spends most of its time in I/O syscalls rather than obfuscated arithmetic. SUB and SPLIT are cheap, low-risk workhorse passes and are weighted broadly so nearly every function receives them, adding instruction-level diversity at negligible overhead. IBR is emphasized on DiversityGain to convert branch structure into indirect dispatch, complementing FLA. ICALL and IGV are kept at moderate weights: reversefile has few indirect-call sites and few global variables, so the security payoff is limited, and CorrectnessRisk is kept slightly higher for ICALL to account for C++ virtual-call and exception-handling interactions that must not be broken.
